task_title: Replace mutable assets/queue with immutable per-change asset request refs

plan_review.notes: Adversarial plan review enumerated three alternatives (append-only request-log branch, Azure/GitHub-issue queue as source of truth, mutable per-request branches) and rejected each; the immutable-ref architecture held. It found four real acceptance-criterion gaps in the implementation: (1) annotation requests had no per-key staleness check, so a stale annotation could overwrite a newer value — fixed with annotationsAt()/per-key comparison; (2) the removal duplicate proof only checked that the surviving shard existed, not that it owned the proven bytes — fixed by verifying the surviving shard's assetPath and contentHash; (3) the conflict fingerprint ignored sourceRun, so materially different requests could collapse as duplicates — fixed by fingerprinting the full canonical entry; (4) the cutover diff covered only public/assets/generated, so a briefs/ delta could survive an apparently complete report — fixed by diffing every legacy queue surface and classifying briefs as requires-human. The sixth concern (add regression tests for each) was implemented: 5 new tests. The fifth concern — production workflows still target assets/queue — is answered by design: repointing ingestion is cutover step 1 and a human action, documented in ADR 0088 and the handoff rather than silently flipped.

rounds.notes: Archive retry hazard: a crash between the archive push and the live-ref delete made the retry fail on an already-existing archive ref. Fixed by checking the archive ref first — identical commit is a no-op, diverged commit throws rather than being force-overwritten. Two regression tests added.

Independent read-only review (different model) after the plan-review fixes — annotation staleness, source-bound removal proof, full-entry conflict fingerprint, briefs classification, queue/check-in snapshot. Verified ref-name construction is non-attacker-controlled, all git calls use execFile array args with no shell interpolation, path validation rejects traversal/absolute/NUL before joining, and the CAS leases prevent silent overwrites. No significant issues found.

independent_grade.notes: The diff implements the transition from a mutable assets/queue aggregate branch to immutable per-change asset request refs according to ADR 0088. It cleanly scopes the changes into new cohesive modules in scripts/sprites/asset-requests and introduces strong typing and hash-based manifest verification. It effectively provides comprehensive test coverage for all new components (manifest, migrate-queue, publish, reconcile, and modified queue-commit for freeze enforcement). Maintainability is excellent with distinct layers of validation, explicit documentation, and minimal footprint in core game behavior (strictly a tooling upgrade). Repo policies around determinism and script configurations are appropriately upheld.
